words.gloss: those things which do not last (accusative)

literal: Those things which do not stand, as permanent things, thus believing, that possession of low wisdom, is the lowest state.
translation: To mistake transient things for permanent realities is the lowest form of ignorance.
modern: நிலைத்து நிற்காத பொருள்களை நிலையானவை என்று நம்புகின்ற சிற்றறிவுடைமை மிக இழிவானதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the lowest level of ignorance, termed 'pullarivanmai' (poor understanding). It occurs when a person mistakes transient, fleeting things (nillathavatrai) for eternal, permanent realities (nilaiyina). The author calls this delusion the lowest state (kadai) of human intellect. Recognizing the impermanent nature of worldly things is the first step toward true wisdom.
